138.92000,-34.34000.name: DIR 201 — GM wheat & barley field trial (yield enhancement)
138.92000,-34.34000.type: GM wheat and barley field trial
138.92000,-34.34000.desc: Field trial of wheat and barley genetically modified for yield enhancement. One site in Light Regional Council, South Australia, maximum two hectares per year, May 2024 to January 2029. Not permitted in human food or animal feed. Location shown at council level — open the licence page for the site conditions.

138.92000,-34.34000.name: DIR 186 — GM wheat & barley field trial (yield + abiotic stress)
138.92000,-34.34000.type: GM wheat and barley field trial
138.92000,-34.34000.desc: Field trial of wheat and barley genetically modified for yield enhancement and improved abiotic stress tolerance. One site in Light Regional Council, South Australia, maximum two hectares per year, April 2022 to January 2027. Licence conditions require isolation from other wheat and barley, secure transport and storage, and end-of-trial destruction verified by site inspection.

143.12737,-38.21597.name: DIR 176 — White clover (Trifolium repens L.) field trial (site 1), Corangamite Shire Council
143.12737,-38.21597.type: White clover (Trifolium repens L.), licensed field trial
143.12737,-38.21597.desc: WHAT. A licensed GMO crop field trial site, Altered condensed tannin concentration, Selectable marker – antibiotic, held by Grasslanz Technology Australia Pty Limited. WHERE IT SITS. OGTR named the council area this site is in and published no coordinate on the page this was read from, so this marker sits in that council area and not at the trial itself. WHY IT MATTERS. OGTR names the council area of every licensed site, its area in hectares and the licence it runs under. No other register on this map states where a release is at all, which is the comparison worth making even at this resolution.

-105.05900,40.57450.name: Rocky Mountain Center for Reproductive Medicine
-105.05900,40.57450.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Kevin E. Bachus, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

19.93817,50.09327.name: TFP Fertility Macierzyństwo
19.93817,50.09327.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-1.68002,48.11134.name: Biotrial Pharmacology
-1.68002,48.11134.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-152.40000,61.37000.name: Wendy Caldwell
-152.40000,61.37000.desc: Breeder registered with USDA APHIS under the Animal Welfare Act, certificate 96-A-0005. Rats, mice and birds bred for research are excluded from the Act's definition of an animal — the overwhelming majority of animals used, and the great majority of the genetically altered ones. What is covered here is dogs, cats, primates, rabbits, guinea pigs, hamsters and farm animals. The rest is counted nowhere.

-113.62794,53.55453.name: Kingfisher International Inc.
-113.62794,53.55453.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, April 2026
-113.62794,53.55453.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, April 2026. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-77.09470,38.98470.name: US Fertility
-77.09470,38.98470.desc: One of the largest fertility clinic groups in the United States, private equity backed, operating dozens of practices under separate local names. The CDC publishes success rates clinic by clinic; it does not publish who owns them, so the consolidation of American fertility care into a few backers is visible only by assembling it from outside the register.

-76.83000,39.16000.name: Intelligence Advanced Research Projects Activity — biology programmes
-76.83000,39.16000.desc: The US intelligence community’s research arm has funded work on reading and attributing engineered biology — determining from a sample whether an organism was made deliberately and by whom. Attribution is the capability that would make any biological rule enforceable, and it is being built inside intelligence rather than inside biosafety.

-17.46000,14.71000.name: Institut Sénégalais de Recherches Agricoles
-17.46000,14.71000.desc: Senegal’s agricultural research institute, working on millet, sorghum and cowpea — the crops of the Sahel, which no multinational breeds for because there is no market to capture. What happens to those crops depends almost entirely on public institutes like this one.
